name: Link Extractor
title: Link Extractor: Pull Every Link From Any Page
description: Free link extractor: get every link on a page — internal vs external, anchor text, nofollow, sponsored, ugc — as a table you can copy or export.
answer: A link extractor pulls every link from a page into a table: URL, anchor text, internal or external, and rel attributes such as nofollow, sponsored and ugc. Enter a URL to see all links, filter them, and export the list as CSV.
trust: We fetch the live HTML and read every a element with an href, exactly as a crawler that doesn't run JavaScript would.
body:
## What does the link extractor show?

Every `<a href>` on the page, one row each, with the details that decide how search engines treat it:

| Column | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| URL | Where the link goes (resolved to an absolute URL) |
| Anchor text | The words Google uses to understand the target |
| Internal / external | Internal links spread authority through your site |
| In navigation | Menu and footer links vs links inside content |
| rel | nofollow, sponsored, ugc — or none |

Download the table as CSV to sort, filter or compare in a spreadsheet.

## Which links can Google follow?

Only real links. Google says it can generally [crawl a link only if it's an a element with an href](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable); links that work only through JavaScript click handlers often go undiscovered. Because we read raw HTML, a link missing here is a link a non-rendering crawler can't see.

## What do nofollow, sponsored and ugc mean?

They're hints about the relationship between you and the page you link to, documented in Google's guide to [qualifying outbound links](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/qualify-outbound-links):

- **sponsored** — paid or affiliate links;
- **ugc** — links in user-generated content such as comments;
- **nofollow** — any other link you don't want to vouch for.

Use them on links that need them, not on your own internal links.

## How should I use the list?

Three quick audits:

1. **Anchor text** — replace "click here" and "read more" with words that describe the target.
2. **Internal links in content** — important pages should get links from body copy, not only menus.
3. **Broken or redirected targets** — paste the URLs into the [HTTP status checker](/tools/http-status-checker).

When we ran it on our own homepage, 48 of its 52 links sat in the navigation and footer and only 4 in the content itself. Template links are fine, but they're the same on every page — contextual links from body copy are what tell Google which pages matter most. For page-level grading, use the [on-page SEO checker](/tools/on-page-seo-checker).

faqs.q: Why are some links on the page missing?
faqs.a: Links created only by JavaScript, or elements without an href, don't exist in the raw HTML. Google may miss them too, which is why it recommends real a elements with href attributes.
No. Nofollow on your own internal links stops signals flowing to your own pages. Reserve nofollow, sponsored and ugc for outbound links that need them.
